questions.q: Which flagship project leans hardest on chunking, retrieval quality, and grounded generation?
options: The production RAG knowledge assistant (Project 1)
The tool-using agent (Project 3)
The AI data analyst (Project 2)
None of the three projects cover retrieval
questions.explain: The lesson states that Project 1, the RAG knowledge assistant, leans hardest on chunking, retrieval quality, and making sure generation is grounded in cited sources.

questions.q: According to this lesson's framework, if you're targeting an applied AI engineer role working with data teams, which project should you polish deepest?
options: Project 3, the tool-using agent
Project 1, the RAG knowledge assistant
Project 2, the AI data analyst (SQL/APIs)
The framework doesn't distinguish between roles
questions.explain: The lesson's role framework maps a data-facing applied AI engineer role to Project 2, since it leans on safe SQL generation and combining structured data sources.

questions.q: What skill set does Project 3, the tool-using agent, lean on hardest per this lesson?
options: Embedding model selection and vector database tuning
Agent orchestration, approval gates, security, and logging
Writing SQL queries against a relational database
Chunking strategy for long documents
questions.explain: The lesson ties Project 3 to agent orchestration plus the operational discipline of approval gates, security, and logging — mapping to agentic / AI platform engineer roles.

questions.q: Does choosing an emphasis mean skipping the other two flagship projects?
options: Yes, you only build the one project matching your target role
Yes, but only if you are already employed as an AI engineer
The lesson does not address this question
No — Project 1 builds first regardless, and emphasis just means which project gets extra polish
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that emphasis is about which project gets the extra polish pass before showing it to an employer, not about skipping the other builds.

questions.q: Why does this course build Project 1 first regardless of a student's target role?
options: Because its evaluation and deployment patterns are reused directly in Projects 2 and 3
Because Project 1 is required for a different, unrelated certification
Because Project 1 takes the least time to build of the three
There is no stated reason in the lesson
questions.explain: The lesson explains that Project 1's patterns — building an eval set, measuring instead of guessing, and deploying behind an API — carry forward directly into Projects 2 and 3.
